newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stena Line sells Harwich Port for 72 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Stena Line sells Harwich Port for 72 mln stg.

text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line said on Tuesday it sold Harwich International Port in Britain for 72 million sterling to a new company financed by HSBC Private Equity Investment Banking in London.
Stena Line said in a statement it would get a capital gain of 150 million crowns from the sale and that its cash reserves would be boosted by 575 million crowns.
"We have been offered an attractive price and are selling Harwich because our main business is shipping, not ports," said Stena Line's managing director Bo Lerenius.
Stena Line said it would continue to use the port as a customer. It operates a large HSS high speed ferry and two freight ships from Harwich to the Hook of Holland.
Lerenius said the sale would strengthen the group's financial position after last year's hefty losses.
Stena Line took control of Harwich International Port, as well as the west coast ports of Fishguard, Holyhead and Stranraer in 1990 when it acquired the then Sealink British Ferries.
Harwich is the largest of these ports and about half of its income comes from external customers.
However Stena Line is the only user of Fishguard and Stranraer and there is only one other customer at Holyhead.
"We have no plans to change our ownership of these as there are so directly integrated into our operations," a company spokesman said.
